items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XVI, List of Answers on Terminology 179:1
items.html: The upper one clarifies from the Klipot only the lower one that is near to his degree. For example, AVI clarify only for ZA, whose sparks are near to AVI, and likewise in all the degrees. And the reason is that the entire matter of the ascent and the correction, by which the lower one is corrected by means of the upper one, is because the AHP of the upper one are always attached to the GE of the lower one, and therefore they are corrected with him, as is known. And this is possible only in the degree adjacent to him, in which his AHP are placed. But not so in the degree below his lower one, with which he has no connection whatsoever. (Item 22).
